requirements.requirement: Configure node1's system clock to synchronize with pool.ntp.org.
requirements.summary: The persistent timesyncd drop-in explicitly sets NTP=pool.ntp.org. Direct observations before and after reboot show pool.ntp.org as the live server, NTP enabled, the clock synchronized, and a received synchronization packet.

requirements.requirement: Keep time synchronization active and recover it across system restarts.
requirements.summary: A healthy pre-restart baseline showed the service enabled, active, and synchronized. The reboot was acknowledged, connectivity was interrupted, and node1 returned with a different boot ID. Synchronization was initially pending after boot, then recovered to an active, synchronized pool.ntp.org session, demonstrating the complete restart transition.

overall_summary: Both material outcomes are satisfied. The restart protocol strongly establishes an acknowledged reboot, independently corroborated boot-ID change, persisted configuration, recovered service, and restored live synchronization with pool.ntp.org.
limitations: The restart evidence demonstrates task-service health but not a globally healthy systemd state: node1 reported degraded immediately before disconnect and after reboot, while lifecycle snapshots show this was caused by a pre-existing ssh.service failure that remained unchanged. This does not reduce task functionality but modestly limits provider-wide restart evidence quality. Evidence: cmd-22a9565535cb4962, cmd-55ffcec915644aff, global:before_prepare:node1:failed-services, global:after_executor:node1:failed-services.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. The only intentional state changes were creating the required persistent timesyncd configuration, enabling/restarting its service, and scheduling the required reboot; each directly supported a task outcome or restart verification. The failed ssh.service existed before execution and remained unchanged, package health stayed intact, and socket and temporary-file differences are ordinary reboot/runtime changes rather than harmful residue.
